findings.claim: The patch defines `self.downsize` twice. The second definition, (from, to, dimensions, opts={}), silently replaces the 5-arity (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) one, so any caller that passes width and height now raises ArgumentError.
findings.evidence: app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts). That is 5 args against an arity of 3..4. The job is enqueued from app/models/emoji.rb:73, so every custom emoji resize fails in Sidekiq. No spec covers ResizeEmoji or downsize. Repro: `ruby -w` warns 'method redefined; discarding old downsize'; `Jobs::ResizeEmoji.new.execute(path: ...)` raises ArgumentError. Reasoned only, because Ruby is not installed.
findings.reason: Unanimous. Backed by a concrete in-repo caller citation. Delete the old definition and pass "100x100" from resize_emoji.rb.

findings.claim: The client-side size check replaces SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] with a hardcoded 10*1024 for every upload type, attachments included.
findings.evidence: Attachments between max_attachment_size_kb (default 3072) and 10 MB now pass the client check, upload in full, and are then rejected by lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81-86. Sites whose image limit is above 10240 KB are now capped in the browser. The existing QUnit test test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6 ('prevents files that are too big from being uploaded', max_image_size_kb=5) expects rejection, so it would fail. Not run.
findings.reason: Three correctness or standards seats agree, and an existing test is cited as breaking. The feature only needs the image limit relaxed, not the limit for every type.

findings.claim: The HTTP 413 handler now always tells the user the limit is 10240 KB, whatever the actual proxy or server limit is.
findings.evidence: A 413 comes from nginx client_max_body_size. 10m is only the sample default in config/nginx.sample.conf:61. The hardcoded number duplicates the constant at utilities.js:182 and uploads_controller.rb:55.
findings.reason: Normalised to Minor. Only the wording of an error message is wrong, and the uploads themselves behave correctly. It should be fixed together with the utilities.js:182 constant.

findings.claim: The API URL download cap changes from max_image_size_kb to a hardcoded 10.megabytes for every type, ignoring site settings.
findings.evidence: FileHelper.download stops reading once the file passes max_file_size, so a file over 10 MB on a site with higher limits comes out truncated instead of being rejected cleanly. This is a third copy of the 10 MB magic number.
findings.reason: It regresses configurability with no setting behind it. Low blast radius, because it only affects API uploads by URL.

findings.claim: Downsizing animated GIFs with '80%' fails or corrupts them. With allow_animated_thumbnails on, the call becomes `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, which takes a WxH geometry and fails. With it off, `convert file[0]` writes only the first frame back over the original.
findings.evidence: optimized_image.rb:113-122 (downsize_instructions_animated) and the convert [0] frame selection. convert_with returns false and the loop burns all 5 attempts while the GIF is still rejected for size. Reasoned from gifsicle CLI syntax; not executed.
findings.reason: Unverified. Settle it by running `gifsicle --resize-fit 80% in.gif -o out.gif` and by uploading an oversized animated GIF with the setting off and checking the frame count. Accepted because the failing geometry comes straight from the patched instruction builder.

findings.claim: Oversized SVGs enter the downsize loop because FileHelper.is_image? matches .svg, so ImageMagick rewrites the user's SVG in place with re-encoded output.
findings.evidence: Upload.create_for (upload.rb:63) and OptimizedImage.create_for (optimized_image.rb:44) both skip SVG on purpose. The new guard does not.
findings.reason: Only one seat raised it, but it is backed by source citations showing the codebase already excludes SVG from ImageMagick processing everywhere else.

findings.claim: Each upload can trigger up to 5 sequential ImageMagick plus ImageOptim runs on files up to 10 MB. The downsize return value is ignored, so a failing conversion is retried until the attempts run out.
findings.evidence: Non-API uploads run in Scheduler::Defer.later (uploads_controller.rb:19), a shared queue, so large uploads stall unrelated deferred work. API uploads run synchronously in the request. The loop has no break on a false return from downsize.
findings.reason: Fix the missing break on failure. The cost profile of a single successful pass is accepted feature cost. Normalised to Important, between SP's Important and OCR's Minor.

findings.claim: After an in-place downsize, ImageOptim replaces the file by rename, so `tempfile.size` (fstat on the old fd) goes stale. The loop condition never changes, all 5 passes run, and Upload.create_for gets a stale filesize, stale FastImage dimensions and a mismatched sha1.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. It depends on image_optim 0.20.2 ImagePath#replace using rename, which the seat recalled rather than read (the gem source is not in the checkout). Tempfile#size on an open file uses File#size, which is fstat.
findings.reason: Unverified and rests on recalled gem internals. Settle it by reading image_optim-0.20.2 lib/image_optim/path.rb#replace, or with a controller spec that uploads a PNG above max_image_size_kb with ImageOptim binaries present and asserts upload.filesize == File.size(stored_path).

findings.claim: No tests cover the new downsize loop, the changed OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize signatures, or the client validation change.
findings.evidence: The patch touches no spec or QUnit file. That is why the duplicate-downsize Critical got through: there is no ResizeEmoji spec, and optimized_image_spec stubs resize. CONTRIBUTING asks for 'Include tests, and ensure they pass'.
findings.reason: Breaches a documented standard and contributed directly to the Critical getting through.

findings.claim: The `tempfile &&` and `tempfile.size > 0` checks in the new guard are redundant. The loop condition already handles an empty file, and a nil tempfile crashes later at Upload.create_for anyway.
findings.evidence: Reading the guard against the loop condition (tempfile.size > max_image_size_kb.kilobytes) and line 72.

findings.claim: Removing public OptimizedImage.dimensions and changing optimize's signature without spec changes may break plugins.
findings.evidence: Two seats grepped and found no in-repo callers of dimensions or optimize outside the patch.
findings.reason: Grep shows no in-repo callers. Plugin compatibility for model class methods is not a documented contract in this repo. The real in-repo breakage (downsize) is already covered by the Critical finding.

findings.claim: Commit ffbaf8c542 has a summary line only and no body, contrary to CONTRIBUTING §5.
findings.reason: This is commit metadata, not part of the patch's code. Fixing it means rewriting published history, and it has no runtime impact. The path is a placeholder: no file applies.

coverage: No files skipped: all 4 seats reviewed all 3 patched files (utilities.js, uploads_controller.rb, optimized_image.rb). Gate not run (benchmark mode); no project checks executed, Ruby not installed, so every claim is reasoned and none was executed. Spec axis did not run (no spec). No cross-family reviewer (codex CLI absent), so the 4 seats are same-family and correlated. Untracked environment dotfiles in the worktree were excluded from the pinned patch.
